_note: Run: python3 bin/mutate.py --spec mutations/aggregate-seeds.json (standard-library-only tests -- no venv needed). These prove tests/test_aggregate_seeds.py's guards are not vacuous. bin/aggregate-seeds.py is the single implementation of BASIC5_FAIR_v1 rule 'seed' (seeds 0,1,2 + mean +/- std): each mutant disables one guard or corrupts the statistic, and a test must catch it. The seed-set and repeat guards each have a test that isolates them (a missing seed for the set guard; a 0,1,2,2 whose set still equals {0,1,2} for the repeat guard), so neither hides behind the other.

targets.label: the standard deviation uses the population divisor n instead of the sample divisor n-1, understating the reported spread over seeds
targets.old: variance = sum((v - m) ** 2 for v in values) / (n - 1)
targets.new: variance = sum((v - m) ** 2 for v in values) / n

targets.label: the failed-run guard is disabled, so a mean is taken over a run that did not succeed
targets.old: failed = [r for r in runs if r["status"] != "ok"]
targets.new: failed = [r for r in runs if False]

targets.label: the single-method guard is disabled, so metrics from different methods are averaged together
the linear_eval-stage guard is disabled, so a pretext-stage number is aggregated as if it were a probe
the repeat-seed guard is disabled, so the same run passed twice is averaged as two seeds (0,1,2,2 whose set is still {0,1,2})
the seed-set guard is disabled, so a mean is taken over the wrong seed set (e.g. only 0,1)
the every-metric-in-every-seed guard is disabled, so a metric missing from one seed is silently averaged over the seeds that have it
